full_judgment:
Part VII: Thereafter said two appeals remained undisposed of four years and in the meantime martial law came and taking ill-advantage thereof he was dispossessed from the "B" scheduled suit property by police force on 10.1.83. Consequently the plaintiff filed an application for amendment of the plaint in Title Appeal No. 107 of 1976. The learned Subordinate Judge allowed the amendment by his order dated 2.5.87. By this amendment the plaintiff prayed for a decree declaring his title to "A" scheduled property by way of exchange and for khas possession and consequently paid ad valorem court fees and made necessary amendment in the plaint and added Deputy Custodian of Enemy Property (L & B) and Secretary, Land Administration Board, Segun Bagicha, Dhaka, as the defendant No. 11 and certain persons as the defendant Nos. 12 to 19. Defendant respondent Nos. 11 to 19 then filed written statement on 16.7.87. 

 6. Let us consider this case from another angle. If Parimal would have sold his property in East Pakistan and in exchange of the sale price he would have obtained the property of the petitioner Hafizur Rahman in India, then could the sale price, if deposited by Hafiz in a bank, be treated as enemy property? The answer is no as money had passed absolutely to Hafiz. But then why the suit property after being given in lieu of the sale-price as exchange should not be deemed to have passed absolutely to Hafiz? Our conclusion following the said principle is that in a case like this when in pursuance of an agreement to transfer property, the intended transferee has taken possession, though the requisite legal document has not been executed, the position is the same as if the document had been executed against all who want to threaten or disturb the possession of such possessor. We, therefore, hold that the plaintiff-petitioner has acquired title to the suit property sufficient to defend his possession therein and to get khas possession thereof, if ousted therefrom. Consequently, we hold that the learned Subordinate Judge committed error in law resulting in error in his decision occasioning failure of justice in not decreeing the suit as prayed for. 

 The result is that both the Rules are made absolute without cost. The analogous judgment and the decrees dated 30.8.90 passed in title Appeal Nos. 107 of 1976 and 140 of 1976 by the learned Subordinate Judge, Khulna, are set aside and the judgment and decree dated 7.5.76 passed in Title Suit No. 122 of 1973 are restored with the modification in the decree to the effect that the plaintiff do get decree for declaration that he has acquired title to the suit property described in schedule "A" in the plaint and for recovery of khas possession thereof after evicting therefrom the defendants and all other persons, if any inducted therein by the defendants, with usual costs against the contesting defendants in addition compensatory cost of Taka 20,000.00 (Taka twenty thousand) to be paid by the defendant No. 1 Deputy Commissioner, Khulna, to the plaintiff. The trial Court is directed to modify its decree accordingly.
